lines.japanese: 夜空を仰ぐと、風に揺れるトチノキの梢が白い月を引っかいていた。
lines.english: I looked up into the night. The wind-tossed crown of the horse chestnut scratched at the white moon.

lines.japanese: むやみに女のひとの体を触ってはいけませんとダヴにこっぴどく叱られてしまった私は、申しわけない気持ちで羽田城の狭き庭に佇んでいた。
lines.english: Dove had given me a serious scolding: you mustn't go around touching women's bodies for no reason. So I stood in Haneda Castle's narrow garden feeling very sorry for myself.

lines.japanese: 言われてみればたしかにその通りだった。
lines.english: Once she said it, I had to concede that she was right.

lines.japanese: 庭履き用の木靴で、マンティコアの額ほどの土の上に立って思う。
lines.english: I contemplated the matter in my garden clogs, standing upon a patch of earth no broader than a manticore's brow.

lines.japanese: どうもゴブリンが人間に見えてしまったり、ホーリーランスが揮わなかったり、奇妙な異世界の記憶を刷りこまれたりと、強引に≪コックピット≫を奪還したせいで大脳機能の運用が芳しくないようだ。
lines.english: Goblin faces appeared human to me, my Holy Lance refused to answer the call, and bizarre memories of other worlds had been stamped into my mind. It appeared that my forcible recapture of the *Cockpit* had left the operation of my higher brain functions in a sorry state.

lines.japanese: いまはまだ巧妙に誤魔化しきれているが、このままではいずれ周囲の者に、精神異常者だと疑われてしまうかもしれない。
lines.english: For now I had managed to disguise the trouble with consummate skill. At this rate, however, those around me might eventually suspect that I was insane.

lines.japanese: これは意識や五感が正常に機能していないせいだ。正しく考えることや正しく見ることが、ノイズの混入によって阻害されているのだろう。
lines.english: My consciousness and five senses were not functioning normally. Noise in the signal must have been keeping me from thinking properly and seeing clearly.

lines.japanese: だがこれまでも、私の考えることや見ることに正しい真理などあっただろうか。いいや、違う、私にはそもそも考える必要さえなかったのだ。
lines.english: But had anything I thought or saw ever contained truth? No. That was wrong. In the first place, I had never even needed to think.

lines.japanese: 以前の私はもっとシンプルで、プリミティブで、オートマティックな存在だった。ただ赤い衝動に任せて目的を遂行するだけだった。
lines.english: I had once been a simpler being: primitive, automatic. I had only to obey the red impulse and carry out my purpose.

lines.japanese: 私の本質は（たとえば撃鉄を引く指にいかなる悪意や逡巡があろうとも、撃ちだされた銃弾は何も思わず何も考えないとしましょう）指ではなく銃弾だったのだ。
lines.english: I had mistaken my nature. A finger may pull back a gun’s hammer with malice or hesitation. The bullet, once fired, neither thinks nor feels. I was the bullet, not the finger.

lines.japanese: しかし永らく奈落の底から地上の光に焦がれていたせいで──竪穴の縁にしがみつき≪世界の声≫を聴いていたせいで──あるいは愚弟たちが赤い衝動を忌むべきものとして封じていたせいで、私は変わってしまった。
lines.english: But perhaps I had yearned too long for the light above from the bottom of the abyss—clung too long to the rim of that vertical shaft, listening to the *voices of the world*. Or perhaps my foolish brothers had sealed the red impulse away too long as a thing to be abhorred. Whatever the cause, I had changed.

lines.japanese: かつてはもっと純粋に、迷うことなく誰かをやっつけてやりたいと思うことができたのに。
lines.english: Once I had been able to want to give someone a sound thrashing with perfect purity, without a moment's doubt.

lines.japanese: 「おのれ！　憎むべきはかの老いぼれ牧師、そして我が愚弟たち！」
lines.english: “Damn them! Damn that decrepit priest—and damn my witless brothers!”

lines.japanese: 凍えた土の上、私はこぶしを握って叫んでみた。しかし、あの赤い帳が下りてこない。
lines.english: Upon the frozen earth I clenched my fists and tried shouting. But the red curtain did not fall.

lines.japanese: 「奈落へ落ちろ！　ハッ！　奈落へ落ちろ！　ハアッ！」
lines.english: “Fall into the abyss! Hah! Fall into the abyss! Haaah!”

lines.japanese: 下りて、こない。
lines.english: It did not... fall.

lines.japanese: 「ふむん、ふむん……」
lines.english: “Hrm. Hrrm...”

lines.japanese: 腕を組み、首をひねった。歌を忘れたカナリヤ。翼の折れた天使。憎しみを失った伊丹伽楼羅。ばほん、つまり、いまの私には存在する価値がないということではないか。
lines.english: I folded my arms and cocked my head. A canary that had forgotten its song. An angel with broken wings. Karura Itami without his hatred. Bah. Did that mean I no longer had any reason to exist?

lines.japanese: 存在する価値がない者は奈落へ落ちる──私は身の凍るような不文律を思いおこした。
lines.english: Those with no reason to exist fall into the abyss. I remembered that unwritten law, and my blood ran cold.

lines.japanese: 過去、幾人もの兄弟たちが生まれては消えていった。みな何らかの役割を持って生まれるが、その役割を果たす必要がなくなれば存在意義を失って深淵の底へ落ちてゆくのだ。
lines.english: Any number of brothers had been born and vanished before me. Each came into being with a role. Once the role was no longer needed, he lost his reason to exist and fell to the bottom of the abyss.

lines.japanese: だから私もふたたび落ちるのだろうか。
lines.english: Then would I fall again as well?

lines.japanese: いや、そうか、違う（皮肉なことですが、いまの私は思索し理解し悔悟し絶望することが出来るようです）。もともと私の果たすべき役割など消滅していたからこそ、私は光すら届かぬ奈落の底に幽閉されていたのだ。
lines.english: No. I understood. That was not it. (The irony is that I now seem capable of reflection, comprehension, remorse, and despair.) I had been imprisoned at the bottom of the lightless abyss precisely because the role appointed to me had already ceased to exist.

lines.japanese: いまさら≪コックピット≫へ返りざいたところで、私の果たすべき役割などありはしなかったのだ。
lines.english: Though I had seized the *Cockpit* again after all this time, no purpose had been waiting there for me.

lines.japanese: ならば、ふたたび引きずりおとされるまでだ。
lines.english: There was nothing left but to be dragged down again.

lines.japanese: どこからともなくおぞましい寒気が忍びよってきて、私は初めての感覚に身を震わせた。
lines.english: A hideous chill crept upon me from nowhere, and I trembled at a sensation I had never known.

lines.japanese: 「嫌だ……もうあそこは嫌だ……」
lines.english: “No... I don't want to go back there...”

lines.japanese: 背中が突っ張って後ろへ反れ、頭が片側へ片側へ傾きはじめる。耳孔からガルーダ・ダークブラックの自我が漏れだしそうだった。
lines.english: My back went rigid and arched; my head began listing to one side, then the other. The self of Garuda Darkblack felt ready to leak out through my ears.

lines.japanese: 「いっ、嫌っ、だ……戻り、たく、ない……！」
lines.english: “N-no... I don't... want to go back...!”

lines.japanese: 私は下向いた耳の穴を塞ぎながら、奈落の引力に抗った。なにか喋っていなければ下顎が震えそうだった。
lines.english: I fought the pull of the abyss, clapping my hands over the ears now tilted toward the ground. If I did not keep talking, my lower jaw would begin to shake.

lines.japanese: 「ふ、不平等ではないか……かか、かつては忌避すべき役割すべて俺に押しつけておきながら、用が済めばもう出てくるなだと……」
lines.english: “I-it isn't fair... Once you forced every loathsome duty upon me, and now that you have no use for me, I am never to come out again...”

lines.japanese: 「か、勝手に産みおとしておいて、用が済めば地獄送りだと……ふざ、ふざけるなァァァ！」
lines.english: “Y-you gave birth to me as you pleased, and once you had used me up, you cast me into hell... D-don't—don't fuck with me!”

lines.japanese: 「飛鳥尽きて長弓蔵められ、狡兎滅して走狗煮らる！　おのれ、冗談ではない！　おい、聞いているのかフェニックス、俺とて友達や妹と隠れんぼをして遊びたいのだ！　いやだよう、戻りたくないよう！」
lines.english: “When the last bird is brought down, the longbow is put away; when the cunning hare is dead, the running hound is cooked! Damn you, this is no joke! Phoenix, are you listening? I want to play hide-and-seek with my friends and little sister too! I don’t want to go back! Please, I don’t want to go back!”

lines.japanese: 嫌だよう！
lines.english: I don't want to!

lines.japanese: ひとりはもう嫌だよう！
lines.english: I don't want to be alone anymore!

lines.japanese: 「みんなと遊びたいよう！」
lines.english: “I want to play with everyone!”

lines.japanese: 「あの……いたみさん……？」
lines.english: “Um... Mr. Itami...?”

lines.japanese: 寒風に吠えていた私を、暖かな場所から呼ぶ声があった。振りかえると、体の半分を雨戸で隠した少女が縁側に立っていた。そして──
lines.english: A voice called from warmth to where I stood howling into the winter wind. I turned. A girl stood on the veranda, half her body hidden behind a storm shutter. And then—
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: ──振りかえった拍子に傾いていた頭が元の平衡を取りもどし、私はいま展開させていた思考を一瞬にしてすべて忘却した。
lines.english: —the act of turning righted my tilted head, and every thought I had been pursuing vanished from my mind in an instant.

lines.japanese: 「ふむん？　はて、なんだ？」
lines.english: “Hrm? Now, what was that?”

lines.japanese: 私はいま何をしていたのか。そう自問したつもりだったが、ダヴが割りこんで答えた。
lines.english: I meant to ask myself what I had just been doing, but Dove cut in and answered instead.

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、３０分ぐらいでおふろが沸くので」
lines.english: “Um, no... I only came to say the bath will be ready in about thirty minutes.”

lines.japanese: 「は、さようでしたか、これは畏れいります」
lines.english: “Ah. I see. You have my thanks.”

lines.japanese: 私は謝罪するように頭を垂れながら、いつの間にやら頬を湿らせていた謎の水気を手の甲で拭いとった。
lines.english: I lowered my head as though apologizing and wiped with the back of my hand the mysterious moisture that had somehow wet my cheeks.

lines.japanese: 羽田城内からは賑わしい若者たちの戯れごとが聞こえてくる。ダヴがテレビジョンに火を灯したのだろう。
lines.english: The lively antics of young people could be heard from within Haneda Castle. Dove must have lit the television.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのっ！　あの、朝ごはんが残ってるんで、あの、食べちゃってくださいっ」
lines.english: “U-um! There's some breakfast left over, so please go ahead and eat it!”

lines.japanese: 「は、いえ、愚生ごときが小鳩様の歓待を受けるなど滅相もございません。私はここで」
lines.english: “No, no. It would be unthinkable for one such as I to accept Lady Kobato's hospitality. I shall remain here—”

lines.japanese: 「え……や、だめです、はやく入ってください」
lines.english: “What...? N-no, you can't. Please come inside.”

lines.japanese: 「はむん、良いのです。私などはしょせん獲物なき平野の猟犬、卑しき牡犬……華やかな宮殿にも温かな茶の間にも立ちいりませぬゆえ、なにとぞ、何卒かの深淵にだけは送りかえしてくださいますな」
lines.english: “Hrm, it is quite all right. I am merely a hunting dog on a plain without prey, a lowly cur. I have no place in a glittering palace or a warm family room. Only, I beg you—send me anywhere but back to the abyss.”

lines.japanese: 「上がってください。日本では薄着で寒いところにいると風邪をひきます」
lines.english: “Please come inside. In Japan, if you stand out in the cold dressed that lightly, you'll catch a cold.”

lines.japanese: 「は、ははぁ！　もったいないお言葉！」
lines.english: “Y-yes! You’re too kind!”

lines.japanese: 不意に目頭が熱くなった。慈悲深き姫君のご尊顔がまばゆくて、私はいっそう頭を深く落としてから改めて背筋を正した。
lines.english: Without warning, my eyes grew hot. Dazzled by the merciful princess's countenance, I bowed still lower before straightening my back anew.

lines.japanese: 「うぉふん……それではお言葉に甘え、すぽんすぽん、馳走にあずからせていただきます」
lines.english: “Hrrumph... Then I shall accept your gracious invitation. Off come the clogs! I will partake of the feast.”

lines.japanese: 庭履きを乱暴に脱ぎすて（行儀良く揃えたりしないのは忌々しい風習に対するせめてもの反抗心である）、板敷きの縁側に体を上げた。ダヴは三重の戸を次々に閉めると、食膳の準備に向かった。
lines.english: I flung aside the garden clogs—my refusal to arrange them neatly was the least rebellion I could offer against this odious custom—and hoisted myself onto the wooden veranda. Dove closed the three layers of doors one after another, then went to prepare the meal.

lines.japanese: 私は畳の間に踏みいり、脚の低いテーブルの一辺にあぐらを組んで座った。テレビジョンの前面ガラスには、巨大な頭部の人間たちが動きまわる電脳紙芝居が映しだされていた。
lines.english: I entered the tatami room and sat cross-legged along one side of the low table. Upon the television's glass face, people with gigantic heads moved through an electronic picture play.

lines.japanese: こら待ちなさーい。うへえ許して姉すゎあーん。巨大な頭部の姉弟が画面の中を走る。その後ろで他の登場人物たちが笑っている。みんなが笑っている。お陽様も笑っている。なぜだか愉快な気分になって私も笑った。
lines.english: *You get back here!* *Uwaah, forgive me, Sisteeer!* The enormous-headed brother and sister ran about inside the screen. The other characters laughed behind them. Everyone laughed. The sun itself laughed. For some reason I began to feel merry, and I laughed too.

lines.japanese: 「ばはは、うっぷはは、ぶっひぶっひ」
lines.english: “Bahaha! Oophahaha! Snort, snort!”

lines.japanese: 「ずわっずわっ、がるがるが、がるがるが、ふいいっしょん、ふいいっしょん」
lines.english: “Wah, wah! Gar-gar-gar, gar-gar-gar! Fwee-choo, fwee-choo!”

lines.japanese: しばらく笑っていると、丸盆に料理と香りを載せたダヴがキッチンから戻ってきた。
lines.english: After I'd laughed for a while, Dove came back from the kitchen with a round tray bearing the food and its delicious smell.

lines.japanese: 主食の白米、溶き玉子のただよう吸い物、焼き魚、根菜の煮物……彼女は器をひとつ卓へ移すごとに、私の表情を怪訝そうに盗み見た。
lines.english: White rice, clear soup with beaten egg drifting through it, grilled fish, simmered root vegetables... As Dove moved each dish from her tray to the table, she stole another puzzled look at my face.

lines.japanese: 「あのう、どうしたんですか」
lines.english: “Um... is something wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「ぶひひ、ご覧の通りですよ、笑っておるのです」
lines.english: “Bweehee. As you see, I am laughing.”

lines.japanese: 「え……泣くほどおもしろいんですか」
lines.english: “Huh...? Is it funny enough to make you cry?”

lines.japanese: ダヴは困ったようにテレビジョンを見詰めた。私はがるがる笑いながら、泣いてなんかないやいと思った（なぜなら鋼の意思を持つグレタガルドの王に、落涙すべきことなんて何ひとつありはしないからです）。
lines.english: Dove stared at the television in perplexity. Laughing my growly *gar-gar-gar*, I thought, *I'm not crying, okay?* (For there is nothing in all creation that could wring tears from the iron-willed king of Gretagard.)

lines.japanese: だが隠さず申さば、心肺機能を鈍らせる得体の知れない違和感が私を苛んでいたのも事実だ。これは……たしかこれは、懐かしいという感情……いや、それだけではない……これは何という感情だったか……。
lines.english: Yet to speak without concealment, it was also true that some nameless unease was oppressing me, slowing my heart and lungs. This was... yes, surely this was the feeling called nostalgia... No, not nostalgia alone. What was the other feeling called...?

lines.japanese: テレビジョンの中のシンプルな絵たちが笑い、ほのぼのとしたリコーダーの楽曲が流れるにつけ、私はいよいよ激しい、暴力的なまでの郷愁と憂鬱に打ちのめされるおのれを自覚していた。
lines.english: The simple drawings on the television laughed, and a gentle recorder tune played. With every moment I became more conscious of the fierce, almost violent nostalgia and melancholy crushing me beneath their weight.

lines.japanese: そう、憂鬱だ。思いだした、この感情は憂鬱と呼ぶんだ。
lines.english: Yes. Melancholy. I remembered now. This feeling was called melancholy.

lines.japanese: 「ぬふん、憂鬱なるかなガルーダ！　ええい、この姉弟の紙芝居はいたずらに私の胸を絞めつける。前向きな情動に冷水を浴びせかける。何故だろう、愉快なはずなのに、暗雲のごとき憂鬱が重くのしかかるわい」
lines.english: “Nnh! Alas, melancholy Garuda! This picture play of brother and sister squeezes my heart. It douses every hopeful feeling. Why does such a merry thing leave a black cloud weighing on me?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、ああ……えっと、日本では日曜日にこの番組を観るとそうゆう気持ちになります」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh... um, in Japan, watching this program on Sunday makes people feel that way.”

lines.japanese: 「なんと、さようでござりますか。うぉんむ、うぉんむ、ならば是非もなし。まこと息苦しく忌々しい悪心であるが、捨ておくよりほかあるまい。ああ落ちつかぬ、また明日学校かあ、嫌だなあ、ぐずぐずん」
lines.english: “What! Is that so? Hrrm, hrrm. Then it cannot be helped. It is a stifling and hateful sickness of the heart, yet I must let it be. Ah, I cannot settle... School again tomorrow. I don't want to go... sniffle, sniffle.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは鼻っ、鼻水をふきんで拭かないでください！」
lines.english: “Y-your nose! Please don't wipe your nose on the dishcloth!”

lines.japanese: 「やや、これはこれは、かたじけのうございます。ぐれっす、ぐれっす！」
lines.english: “Oh! How very kind. My thanks. Gress, gress!”

lines.japanese: ダヴが差しだした鼻紙で顔を拭う。
lines.english: I wiped my face with the tissue Dove held out to me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、はやく食べてください」
lines.english: “Um, please hurry and eat.”

lines.japanese: 私は並べられた簡素な（むろん宮廷料理に比べての話である）食事に箸を通した。とても美味しくて頬が落ちそうになった（ちなみに頬が落ちるというのは、実際に顔面の皮膚が焼けただれることでとても痛いです）。
lines.english: I set my chopsticks to the simple meal laid before me—simple by comparison with court cuisine, naturally. It was so delicious that my cheeks nearly fell off. (Incidentally, when one's cheeks truly fall off, the skin of the face burns and sloughs away, which is extremely painful.)

lines.japanese: 扱いなれない二本の棒に苦戦しながら辛うじて食事を進めていると、対面に正座していたダヴが繕うような咳払いをして背筋を伸ばした。
lines.english: I struggled with the two unfamiliar sticks, managing to eat by degrees. Across from me, Dove sat properly on her knees. She straightened her back and gave a little cough, as though bracing herself.

lines.japanese: 「……お、お味はいかがですか」
lines.english: “...H-how does it taste?”

lines.japanese: 「は。この城は良い調理師をお抱えのようですな。とても美味しゅうございますぞ」
lines.english: “Ah. This castle appears to retain an excellent cook. It is most delicious indeed.”

lines.japanese: 「出来たてならもっと美味しかったです」
lines.english: “It would have tasted better when it was fresh.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむん、しかり。たしかに素材も味付けも素晴らしいが、鮮度に欠けている点は否めませんな。ワニの肉がないのも感心できません。料理は城の顔ゆえ、調理師には厳しく申しつけておくことです」
lines.english: “Hrm, quite. The ingredients and seasoning are superb, certainly, but one cannot deny the lack of freshness. Nor can I approve of the absence of crocodile meat. Cuisine is the face of a castle; you must speak sternly to the cook.”

lines.japanese: 「ところで、姫はお召しあがりにならないので？」
lines.english: “But tell me, Princess, will you not eat?”

lines.japanese: 私の問いに彼女は小さく頷き、さらに体を浮かせて居住まいを正した。
lines.english: At my question she gave a small nod, then lifted herself and settled into an even more formal posture.

lines.japanese: 「たっ、食べながら、聞いてください」
lines.english: “P-please listen while you eat.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 子供だてらに王族の威厳を保とうとしている声と表情が微笑ましかった。私はしなびた青菜を味わいながら短く頭を下げた。
lines.english: The voice and expression with which a mere child strove to preserve royal dignity were charming. I dipped my head briefly while savoring a wilted leaf of greens.

lines.japanese: 「今日は日曜日で時間があったので、私はいつもよりがんばって朝ごはんを作りました」
lines.english: “Today is Sunday, so I had time. I tried harder than usual when I made breakfast.”

lines.japanese: 「なんと！　この膳を小鳩様が手ずから？」
lines.english: “What! Lady Kobato prepared this entire meal with her own hands?”

lines.japanese: 「そうです。だから私は怒っています」
lines.english: “Yes. That is why I'm angry.”

lines.japanese: 「こ、これは失礼いたしました。先ほどの失言、深くお詫び申しあげます」
lines.english: “I-I beg your pardon. Please accept my deepest apologies for my careless remarks.”

lines.japanese: 私はあぐらを組んだ膝の上にそれぞれこぶしを載せ、上半身を深々と折りまげた。
lines.english: I planted my fists upon my crossed knees and bent deeply at the waist.

lines.japanese: 「いや、その、ワニなどなくとも構わんのです。なにぶん私の舌は時代から取りのこされておるゆえ、恥ずかしながら当世の調理というものが理解できず、ついなりたなりたと失言の数々……」
lines.english: “No, truly, the lack of crocodile is of no consequence. My palate has been left behind by the age, and to my shame I understand nothing of modern cookery. In my ignorance I kept stammering and stumbling from one remark to the next...”

lines.japanese: 「まったく重ね重ねのご無礼、平にご容赦くだされ。このガルーダ、いかなる罰でも受ける覚悟にございます、なんなりとお申しつけください」
lines.english: “I have insulted you over and over. I humbly beg your forgiveness. This Garuda stands prepared to accept any punishment. Command me as you will.”

lines.japanese: 「違います。そのことじゃないです」
lines.english: “That's not it. I'm not angry about that.”

lines.japanese: 「ふ、ふむん？」
lines.english: “H-hrm?”

lines.japanese: 「きょ、きょうの朝、起こしに行ったら部屋に誰もいなかったので、私はたいへんびっくりしたのです」
lines.english: “Th-this morning, I went to wake you and found nobody in the room. I was terribly surprised.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おお、さようでしたか。まったく申しわけない」
lines.english: “Oh! I see. You have my sincerest apologies.”

lines.japanese: わけが分からなかったが、ダヴが怒りを抱いていると主張するものだから謝罪するほかなかった。なぜなら私は──我々は──生まれたときからずっと、彼女の心身の平穏を護るべく義務付けられているからです。
lines.english: I had no idea what she meant, but Dove insisted that she was angry, so I could do nothing but apologize. For from the moment of my—our—birth, we had been charged with protecting the peace of her mind and body.

lines.japanese: 「む、むだん外泊はいけないことです。日本では家族のひとが心配をします」
lines.english: “Y-you mustn't stay out all night without telling anyone. In Japan, that makes your family worry.”

lines.japanese: 「とくに皆さんの中には、むかし……とと、とんそう？　え、えっと、なんか記憶そう失みたくなって、何日も行方不明になっちゃったひととかいるので、今でも私たちやお医者の先生はたいへん心配に思っています」
lines.english: “Especially because one of you once... went into a f-fugue? Um, like losing your memory, and disappeared for days. Even now, we and the doctor worry about all of you.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はあ」
lines.english: “Ah. Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「夜、おしごとで出かけるのは仕方ありません。でも朝までには戻ってきてもらわないと困ります。やむを得ない場合はせめて一本れんらくをください」
lines.english: “If work makes you go out at night, that can't be helped. But you have to come home by morning. If you really can't, then at least call us.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、はあ」
lines.english: “Yes. Yes.”

lines.japanese: 私は頭を下げながら適度に同意を挟んだ。
lines.english: I kept my head bowed and inserted agreement at appropriate intervals.

lines.japanese: 「うぉふん、しかし畏れながら姫、その義務を怠ったのは私ではありませんぞ。おそらく夜の戦士、暗黒街の王、愚弟ファルコンですな」
lines.english: “Hrrumph. With all respect, Princess, I was not the one who neglected that duty. The culprit was surely Falcon, warrior of the night and king of the underworld—my foolish brother.”

lines.japanese: 「へりくつを言うのもいけません。皆さんは共存することを選んだのですから、れんたい責任です」
lines.english: “You mustn't argue technicalities either. All of you chose to *coexist*, so you share the responsibility.”

lines.japanese: 「ぐ、ぐむん……」
lines.english: “G-grrm...”

lines.japanese: 「皆さんの問題は、私たち家族の問題でもあります。とくにいまはお父さんもお母さんもいないので──」
lines.english: “Your problems are our family's problems too. Especially now, when Father and Mother are both away—”

lines.japanese: 「なに、ここの城主夫妻が？　けしからん、そやつらは幼き姫君を置いてどこへ消えたのです」
lines.english: “What! The lord and lady of this castle? Outrageous! Where have those two vanished to, leaving a young princess behind?”

lines.japanese: 「旅行に行っています」
lines.english: “They're on a trip.”

lines.japanese: 「旅行とな！　な、なんと呆れた後見人どもだ、王族の者を預かる身で何を安穏と！」
lines.english: “A trip! Wh-what disgraceful guardians! Charged with the care of royalty, and they go idling off—”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ。お父さんとお母さんは、病気についての勉強が忙しかったり目が離せなかったりで、何年もずっとふたりで出かけることが出来なかったのです」
lines.english: “No. Father and Mother were always busy studying the illness and keeping watch over everyone, so for years they couldn't go anywhere alone together.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、さようであったか……あふぅむ、我らのこの特異な体質のせいで、彼らには多大な迷惑をかけてしまったのやもしれんな」
lines.english: “Ah, I see... Hrrm. Our peculiar constitution may have caused them a great deal of trouble.”

lines.japanese: 「でも千歳さんが、さいきんは症状が安定しているから保ご者がいなくても大丈夫とゆうので、お父さんたちには数年ぶりに夫婦みず入らずで出かけてもらうことになりました」
lines.english: “But Mr. Chitose said the symptoms have been stable lately and everyone would be all right without a guardian. So, for the first time in years, Mother and Father went away together with no one else along.”

lines.japanese: ダヴは私と目を合わせず、用意された原稿でも読みあげるように、畏まった口調で淡々と続けた。
lines.english: Dove did not meet my eyes. She continued in a stiff, measured tone, as though reading aloud from a prepared script.

lines.japanese: 「そうゆうわけなので、えと、お父さんたちがいないあいだは私が皆さんの保ご者とゆうことになります。いま皆さんが何かしでかしてしまうと、わた、私のせきにん問題になります」
lines.english: “So, um, while they're away, that makes me everyone's guardian. If any of you gets into trouble now, i-it becomes my responsibility.”

lines.japanese: 「うぉんむ、うぉんむ、なるほどなるほど」
lines.english: “Hrrm, hrrm. I see, I see.”

lines.japanese: 「いやしかし、それなら心配ご無用。この私が≪コックピット≫に入った以上、もう他の者にこの体を明けわたすつもりはございません。イーグルの言葉を借りるなら、私は揺るぎなき安定を得たのです」
lines.english: “But in that case, you have nothing to fear. Now that I occupy the *Cockpit*, I have no intention of surrendering this body to anyone else. To borrow Eagle's words, I have attained an unshakable stability.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: しばらく視線を落としていたダヴが、水面へ呼吸しにきた鯉のように上を向いて口を開けた。もはもはと私は微笑んでみせた。
lines.english: Dove, who had kept her eyes lowered for some time, raised her face and opened her mouth like a carp surfacing to breathe. I gave her a broad, placid smile.

lines.japanese: 「もはもは、ですから、この体は永遠に私ひとりのものとなったのですよ。もはは、ご安心召され、煩わしい交替など金輪際起こりませぬゆえ」
lines.english: “Heh heh. You see, this body is mine alone for all eternity. Mwahaha, be at ease. Those tiresome changes shall never occur again.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、うそ……」
lines.english: “What? That can't be true...”

lines.japanese: 「もはほほほ、私が嘘を申しても仕方ありますまい」
lines.english: “Mwahahaha. What cause would I have to lie?”

lines.japanese: 私の確固たる笑顔とは裏腹に、彼女は言葉を探しあぐねて小さく口を開閉させていた。
lines.english: In contrast to my unshakable smile, she opened and closed her little mouth, unable to find any words.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ、あの……ほ、他のひとは？」
lines.english: “Th-then, um... wh-what about the others?”

lines.japanese: 「他のひと？　ぬふん、愚弟たちなら、もう二度と揚がってくることはないでしょうなあ。いまはまだ待機室にでも引っかかっておるでしょうが、直に奈落の引力に捕われ闇の底へと落ちるでしょうよ。ばふん」
lines.english: “The others? Nnh. If you mean my witless brothers, they will never rise again. For now they may still be caught somewhere in the *Waiting Room*, but the gravity of the abyss will soon seize them and drag them down into the dark. Bah.”

lines.japanese: 私は不快を押しころして答えた。貴き姫君が簒奪者たる愚弟たちの消息を案ずるのは面白くないが、なにぶん心優しき少女ゆえ、ジャムを塗ったパンが床に落ちたときほどの悲しみは感じてしまうのも無理はない。
lines.english: I smothered my displeasure as I answered. A noble princess worrying after my usurping brothers was hardly agreeable, but she was a tenderhearted girl. One could not blame her for feeling sorrow on the scale of seeing jam-covered bread fall face-first upon the floor.

lines.japanese: 「そんな……」
彼女は子供らしい柔らかそうな眉をひそめて私を見上げた。
lines.english: Her soft, childish brows drew together as she looked up at me.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、お兄ちゃんは？　私のお兄ちゃんは？」
lines.english: “Then what about my brother? What about my brother?”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ、ホーク・シアンブルー──羽田タカシの所在ですか。むろん彼とて例外ではなく……」
lines.english: “Hrm. You mean Hawk Cyan-Blue—Takashi Haneda? Naturally, he is no exception—”

lines.japanese: 「ちがう！　そのひとじゃなくて、ほんとのお兄ちゃん！」
lines.english: “No! Not him—my real brother!”

lines.japanese: ダヴがてのひらを勢いよくテーブルに張りつけた。予想外に大きな音がして、私は箸の先を大根の煮物に突きさしたまま固まった。
lines.english: Dove slapped her palm hard against the table. The bang was louder than I expected, and I froze with my chopsticks still stuck in a slice of simmered daikon.

lines.japanese: 「は……？　誰ですと？」
lines.english: “What...? Who did you say?”

lines.japanese: 「私のほんとのお兄ちゃん！　最初からいたひと！　一番目のひと！」
lines.english: “My real brother! The one who was there from the beginning! The first one!”
“The first...?”

lines.japanese: 「そう！　羽田鷹志！」
lines.english: “Yes! Takashi Haneda!”

lines.japanese: 彼女は腰を浮かせ、苛立ちの滲んだ声でその名を挙げた。
lines.english: She half-rose from her seat and said the name with irritation leaking into her voice.

lines.japanese: 「な、んと……ハネダ、ヨージ、とは……」
lines.english: “Wh... what... Haneda... Yoji...”

lines.japanese: 私は思わずうめき、すると頭が片側に傾いて、その拍子に失われていた記憶が突如よみがえった。
lines.english: A groan escaped me. My head listed to one side, and in that motion the memory I had lost came suddenly back.

lines.japanese: 「う、うう……く、先代の、こと、か……」
lines.english: “U-ugh... y-you mean... the former king...”

lines.japanese: 私がとうに脳の隅へ追いやっていたその名を、彼女は希望にすがる必死な声で叫んだのだ。
lines.english: She had cried out the name I had long ago banished to a corner of my mind, her desperate voice clinging to hope.

lines.japanese: 聖騎士コンドル。前グレタガルド王。我らが父。ダヴが言うところの一番目のひと。言うなれば、この体の本来の持ち主。いいや、だが、しかしあの方は──
lines.english: Holy Knight Condor. Former king of Gretagard. Our father. The one Dove called the first. One might say the original owner of this body. No—but then, His Majesty—

lines.japanese: 「──しかしあの方は生を営むことに絶望され、はるか昔に自ら奈落の底へ旅立たれておいでだ。よしんばこちらから招いたとて、二度と≪コックピット≫へはお上がりにならぬでしょう」
lines.english: “—But His Majesty despaired of the business of living and journeyed by his own will to the bottom of the abyss long ago. Even if we called to him from here, he would never ascend to the *Cockpit* again.”

lines.japanese: そう。彼が王位を降りてしまったからこそ、これまで我々──ダヴが言うところの二番目以降──が空いた玉座を埋めてきたのだ。
lines.english: Yes. Because he had abdicated the throne, we—the second and all who came after, as Dove called us—had taken turns filling the empty seat.

lines.japanese: 「でも私はお兄ちゃんに会いたい！」
lines.english: “But I want to see my brother!”

lines.japanese: 永年抑えていた奔流が堰を切ってしまったのか、ダヴは目に涙を溜めて幼い悲痛を露わにした。
lines.english: As though a torrent held back for years had broken its dam, Dove's eyes filled with tears and laid bare the anguish of a child.

lines.japanese: しばし唇を噛みしめて顎の下に硬い皺を作っていたが、やがて癇癪を起こしたようにテーブルを叩いた。
lines.english: For a time she bit her lip, carving a hard crease beneath her chin. Then she struck the table as though throwing a tantrum.

lines.japanese: 「出して！　お兄ちゃん出して！」
lines.english: “Bring him out! Bring my brother out!”

lines.japanese: 「出ーしーてーっ！」
lines.english: “Bring—him—out!”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうは申されても……それはおそらく無理かと……いや、無理ですとも」
lines.english: “E-even if you say so... I fear that is probably impossible... No. It is impossible.”

lines.japanese: 第一に、あの方は自らの意志で闇の世界に閉じこもっている。
lines.english: First: His Majesty had shut himself within the realm of darkness by his own will.

lines.japanese: 第二に、帰還の意志があったとしても奈落からの脱出は限りなく不可能に近い。
lines.english: Second: even if he wished to return, escape from the abyss was all but impossible.

lines.japanese: そして第三に、そもそも私自身が二度と奈落へ帰るつもりはないのだ（言うまでもなく、私にとって他人に≪コックピット≫を明けわたすとは自らをふたたび奈落へ落とすことだ）。
lines.english: And third: I myself had no intention whatsoever of returning to the abyss. (Needless to say, surrendering the *Cockpit* to another would mean casting myself into it once more.)

lines.japanese: 「でも、いたみさん、なんでもって言ったよ」
lines.english: “But Mr. Itami, you said you'd do anything.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は長袖の肘で赤く濡れた目を拭いながら、懇願するような涙声で言った。
lines.english: She wiped her wet, reddened eyes with the elbow of her long sleeve and spoke through pleading tears.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「さっき、なんでも罰受けるって言った」
lines.english: “You said before that you'd accept any punishment.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、たしかに申したが……しかし、むむ……いやしかし、それだけは……」
lines.english: “W-well, yes, I did say that... But, hrm... even so, anything but that...”

lines.japanese: 「うそつき」
lines.english: “Liar.”

lines.japanese: 聞きわけない子供の批難が、偉大なる王の尊厳に小さな擦過傷を与えた。
lines.english: The accusation of an unreasonable child left a tiny scratch upon the dignity of a mighty king.

lines.japanese: 瞬間、私は苛立ちを覚えた気もするが、刺しこむような鋭い頭痛に見舞われたため定かではない。
lines.english: For an instant I may have felt irritation, though a sharp pain stabbed into my head before I could be certain.

lines.japanese: 「返して」
lines.english: “Give him back.”

lines.japanese: めまい。
lines.english: Vertigo.

lines.japanese: 「私のお兄ちゃん返せ！」
lines.english: “Give me back my brother!”

lines.japanese: むかつき。
lines.english: Nausea.

lines.japanese: 「この……にせものっ！」
lines.english: “You... impostor!”

lines.japanese: 「えぇぅ！」
lines.english: “Eeuugh!”

lines.japanese: 胃がねじれて吐き気が込みあげ、そして、ふと瞬きした刹那の世界には赤い帳が下りていた。
lines.english: My stomach twisted and nausea surged up. Then, in the instant of a single blink, the red curtain fell across the world.

lines.japanese: 首がねじれ、背がねじれ、朱に染まった部屋は水面に映った鏡像のように震えて揺れ──するとダヴの幼い少女の体もたちまち醜く膨れあがった。
lines.english: My neck twisted, my back twisted, and the scarlet room shivered and swayed like a reflection on water. Before my eyes, Dove's little-girl body swelled into something hideous.

lines.japanese: 愛らしいふたつの眼を縁取る陰影が、色濃く不気味に滲みだしてゆく。まなじりの際立ったアホウドリのような眼は、けばけばしい道化の隈取りに覆われていった。
lines.english: The shadows framing her two lovely eyes deepened and spread in sinister stains. Her glaring, albatross eyes disappeared beneath the gaudy paint of a clown.

lines.japanese: そのおぞましさに我が目を疑った。馬鹿な。あれは錯覚だ、もしくは絵だ。そうだ、見ろ。なりたなりたと姦しい仔オークの切り絵が、私の正面で滑稽に両腕を上げ下げしているじゃないか。
lines.english: The horror of it made me doubt my eyes. Absurd. It was an illusion, or else a picture. Yes—look. A noisy paper cutout of a little orc was flapping both arms ridiculously before me, yammering away.

lines.japanese: 私はその目障りな絵を破りすてたくて、ハサミかナイフを探した。よく見ればたまたま右手に、先端の尖った棒を二本握っていた。
lines.english: I wanted to rip the eyesore apart and searched for scissors or a knife. Looking closer, I discovered that I happened to be holding two pointed sticks in my right hand.

lines.japanese: ようし、これであの絵に穴を開けてしまおう。うふふ、目玉の辺りが突きごろだ。
lines.english: Excellent. I would punch holes in the picture with these. Heh heh. Right around the eyes looked ripe for stabbing.

lines.japanese: 「ぶふっ……ぶひ、ぶひひ、ぶほはズワアァァァ！」
lines.english: “Bhoof... bwee, bwehehe, bwoha-ZWAAAAAAH!”

lines.japanese: 気合一閃、私は鉄串を振りかぶった。だが──
lines.english: With a burst of resolve, I raised the iron skewer overhead. But—

lines.japanese: 「せっ、世界が平和でありますように！」
lines.english: “M-may peace prevail on Earth!”

lines.japanese: ──こちらが畳を蹴るより速く、敵は緊縛の呪文を唱えた。
lines.english: —before I could kick off from the tatami, my enemy cast the spell of binding.

lines.japanese: 「ぬくッッッ！？」
lines.english: “Nghhh!?”

lines.japanese: 腰を浮かして飛びだした躍動感あふれる体勢のまま、私の大腿筋は不可解な麻痺状態に陥った。
lines.english: Half risen and poised to spring, I found every muscle in my thighs seized by an inexplicable paralysis.

lines.japanese: 「くゥゥゥ！　キ、サ、マァァァ……！」
lines.english: “Gghhh! Y-youuuu...!”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ごっ、ごめ、ごめんなさい！」
lines.english: “Ah... I-I'm sorry, I'm sorry!”

lines.japanese: そのとき不意に、仔オークの肥満した体が揺れた。いや、オークだけではない。視界の隅から隅までもが、あたかも水面に映る鏡像のように震えて揺れはじめたのだ。
lines.english: Then the little orc's bloated body suddenly wavered. No—not the orc alone. My vision began to tremble and sway from corner to corner, like a reflection upon water.

lines.japanese: なんだ……なんだこの幻惑は。
lines.english: What... What manner of enchantment was this?

lines.japanese: 私は一度眼を閉じることで（不本意にも）慣れしたしんできた闇を呼びおろし、ひと呼吸、そしてまた眼を開けた。
lines.english: I closed my eyes, summoning the darkness with which I had become—against my will—so terribly familiar. One breath. Then I opened them again.

lines.japanese: すると、ダヴが居心地悪げに視線を泳がせながら、ささやかに鼻をすすっていた。
lines.english: Dove was sniffling softly, her gaze wandering with discomfort.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんて、えへ、冗談です。びっくりさせてごめんなさい」
lines.english: “Th-that was... heh... only a joke. I'm sorry I startled you.”
“Princess...?”

lines.japanese: ああそうか。私はふと我に返って状況を思いだした。改めて周囲を見回すと、オークの子供はすでに姿をくらましていた。逃げ足の速いやつだ。
lines.english: Ah, yes. I suddenly returned to myself and remembered the situation. Looking around again, I saw that the orc child had already vanished. A quick little creature.

lines.japanese: 「え、え、うぉふん……」
lines.english: “Ah, er—ahem...”

lines.japanese: 私は嘔吐感を堪えて座りなおし、ぶもぶもと口ごもった。
lines.english: I fought down the nausea, sat back up, and went, ‘Mrrph, mrrph...’

lines.japanese: 「姫、そのう、私は……」
lines.english: “Princess, I...”

lines.japanese: 「うん。分かってます。お兄ちゃんは自分から引きこもってるんです。いたみさんも他のみんなも悪くないんです。なのに私はみんなを恨んじゃうやな子です。私がやな子だからばちが当たったんです」
lines.english: “Yes. I know. My brother is hiding because he wants to. Mr. Itami and the others haven’t done anything wrong. But I still resent all of you. I’m a horrible girl. This happened because I’m horrible, and now I’m being punished.”

lines.japanese: 「私がいい子にしてればいいことが待ってるって、牧師さんよく言ってました。だからきっと、お兄ちゃんが出てこなくなっちゃったのは、私がいい子じゃないせいなんです」
lines.english: “The priest used to tell me that if I was good, good things would be waiting for me. So my brother must have stopped coming out because I wasn't a good girl.”

lines.japanese: 「ふ、ふむん……」
lines.english: “H-hrm...”

lines.japanese: そうか、可哀想なプリンセス・ダヴ。醜い仔オークの闖入で失念してしまったが、この子はいま、幼いころに生きわかれた兄と逢いたがっていたのだっけ。
lines.english: I see. Poor Princess Dove. The intrusion of that hideous little orc had driven it from my mind, but this child had been longing to see the brother from whom she was parted when she was small.

lines.japanese: 彼女の力になりたいなあと私は思った。いつもいつも誰かをやっつけてやりたいとばかり思っていた私にも、たまには誰かを喜ばせてあげることが出来ないものだろうか。無理かなあ。でも助けてあげたいなあ。
lines.english: I wanted to help her. I had spent so long wanting to give someone a thrashing. Could I, just once, make someone happy instead? Maybe not. But I wanted to help.

lines.japanese: そんな柄にもないことを考えてしまったせいで、私は自らの存在が薄くなってゆくのを感じた（霞んでゆく目で自分の消えかけた指先を見詰めていると、とてもせつない気持ちになりました）。
lines.english: The thought was so foreign to my nature that I felt my own existence begin to fade. (Watching my fingertips disappear through dimming eyes made me terribly sad.)

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのっ！　そだ、おふ、おふろ見てきます。そろそろ沸いたと思います！」
lines.english: “U-um! Oh, right—the bath! I'll go check the bath. It should be ready by now!”

lines.japanese: ダヴが視線を逸らしたまま部屋を出ていった。可愛いダヴ。兄思いの妹。あの子は必ずや魅力的な女性に育つだろうなあと思いながら、私は廊下へ消えてゆく小さな背中を見送った。
lines.english: Dove left the room without looking at me. Darling Dove. A little sister devoted to her brother. I watched her small back vanish into the hall, thinking what a charming woman she would surely become.

lines.japanese: 「姫、料理の腕を上げましたな。ワニ肉などなくとも、まことに美味しゅうございましたぞ」
lines.english: “Princess, your skill in the kitchen has improved. Crocodile or no, the meal was truly delicious.”

lines.japanese: 箸を置いて手を合わせる。
lines.english: I laid down my chopsticks and pressed my palms together.

lines.japanese: そして私は逝くことにした。
lines.english: And then I resolved to die.

lines.japanese: 「小鳩様、しばしお待ちください。御身のささやかな願い、我が身に代えても叶えてみせましょう」
lines.english: “Lady Kobato, wait but a little while. Your modest wish I shall grant, though I must give myself in exchange.”

lines.japanese: なぜなら私は──我々は──彼女を悲しませないために生まれてきた存在なのだから。
lines.english: For I—we—had been born so that she would never grieve.

lines.japanese: そのことを思いだした私にもはや迷いはなかった。たとえそれが、ふたたびこの身を無間地獄へ落とすことに他ならないとしても。
lines.english: I remembered what we were for, and all my hesitation vanished. Even if it meant casting myself back into the hell of ceaseless torment.

lines.japanese: 私はひとり残された部屋で、食卓に額を付けて頭をもたせた。
lines.english: Alone in the room, I rested my forehead on the dining table and let my head go slack.

lines.japanese: そして私の≪精髄≫はかつての忌まわしい引力に乗り、闇の竪穴を自ら滑りおちていった。
lines.english: Then my *essence* surrendered itself to that hateful old gravity and went sliding down the dark vertical shaft.

lines.japanese: ああ、すまないフェニックス。許せレイヴン。明日の約束は反古になってしまった。童貞のまま先立つ不幸をお許しください。
lines.english: Ah, forgive me, Phoenix. Pardon me, Raven. Our promise for tomorrow has come to nothing. Forgive the tragedy of my going before you while still a virgin.

lines.japanese: 遺言１。さらば友よ！
lines.english: Last testament, the first: farewell, my friends!

lines.japanese: 遺言２。小鳩様万歳！
lines.english: Last testament, the second: long live Lady Kobato!

lines.japanese: 遺言３。グレタガルドに幸あれ！
lines.english: Last testament, the third: fortune upon Gretagard!

lines.japanese: （──伊丹伽楼羅。奈落より愛を込めて）
lines.english: (—Karura Itami. With love from the Abyss.)
